question_text: What are the columns of Bertin?

steps.label: What they are
steps.why: The cortex does not stop at the edge of the medulla: it dips inward between the pyramids, and those dips are the columns.
common_mistakes: Calling them part of the medulla. They are cortex tissue.
Confusing them with renal pyramids. The columns lie between the pyramids.
steps.memory_tip: Cortex reaching down between the pyramids.
steps.margin_note: One sentence carries both marks if it is complete.
lines: The columns of Bertin, also called renal
columns, are the projections of the cortex
into the medulla of the human kidney.

steps.label: What they do
steps.why: By running down between the cones of medulla they keep each pyramid a separate drainage unit.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the pyramids. Separating them is the point.
Writing that they filter blood. They do not.
steps.memory_tip: They are the walls that keep the pyramids apart.
steps.margin_note: One line on what they separate.

lines.text: They separate the renal pyramids from each other

insider_note: This question is asked more often than any other two-mark question in the chapter. The marking words are 'projections of the cortex into the medulla'.
